walkthroughs.body_html:
Fundamentals Of Computer Systems — a core area of A-Level Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Fundamentals Of Computer Systems brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Fundamentals Of Computer Systems.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the main advantage of asymmetric encryption?
options: Secure key exchange without sharing a secret in advance.
It is faster than symmetric encryption.
It is impossible to break.
It can store data permanently.

mcqs.q: What does it mean that RAM is volatile?
options: Its contents are lost when power is removed.
It can explode or be damaged easily.
It can store data permanently.
They produce different programming languages.

mcqs.q: What is the key difference between a compiler and an interpreter?
options: A compiler translates the whole program first; an interpreter executes line by line.
A compiler is a person, an interpreter is software.
They produce different programming languages.
It can store data permanently.
